title: How to play
intro:
**Horseless Carriage: How to play**

Two guided years at the works, against two rival industrialists, Robin and Sam.

steps.welcome: Welcome to the works, director. Nobody knows yet what a horseless carriage should be. Fast? Safe? Pretty? Every year the public changes its mind, and we will chase it.
steps.goal: Money is the only scoreboard. Every dollar we earn shows beside our name, and when the clock runs out, the richest company wins. Everything I show you today is a way of turning a car into a dollar.
steps.chain: Here is the whole business in one breath. Buyers want cars with certain specs. Specs come from stations in our factory. Stations come from research. So every year we research, then build, then sell, in that order.
steps.market: This is the market. Each square is a niche: a corner of the public with its own taste. The cars standing on it are buyers, waiting for a car they like. Four of them today, all in the bottom-left corner.
steps.market-types: Every buyer today wants a plain car. In the full game some want trucks or sports cars, which pay more but need a mainline of their own. This first game is cars only.
steps.axes: What does a buyer want? Read the axes. Today the public cares about two things: safety, along the bottom, and reliability, up the side. The further a niche sits from the bottom-left, the more of each it demands.
steps.axes-why: The buyers in the bottom-left ask for very little. Three of them ask for nothing at all: any car will do. This one wants one reliability, the one box beside its row. That is why we start down here. The niche at the top-right wants three of each, and nobody can build that car yet. When somebody can, it will pay the most.
steps.tracks: These are the research tracks: five things a car can be good at. Only two of them are on the market at a time, the two along the board. The other three wait here, out of fashion for now.
steps.tracks-slots: Each track has six slots, and each slot pictures a station. Reach a slot, and we may build that station in our factory. That is all research is: the right to build something.
steps.tracks-markers: This is your marker on each track; the blue ones are Robin's and the purple ones Sam's: our rivals. On the two tracks on the market, everybody starts on the first slot: the brake and the battery are common knowledge, and anybody may build them. On the three tracks off the board, everybody starts at the start spot, knowing nothing.
steps.office: The planning office keeps the order of play, and order is money. Whoever builds first takes the last station in the supply. Whoever sells first takes the best buyer. I will show you how the order is set when we set it.
steps.factory: And this is your factory. The floor is black, and we may build on any black square. The loading bay in the corner is not black: everything we build must connect to it, one tile touching the next, so that the cars can get out of the building.
steps.departments: Two departments are already on your floor. The research department gives you one research step a year. The planning department earns you a Gantt chart a year, and Gantt charts decide who chooses first. Both only need to touch the bay, or a tile that does.
steps.supply: Stations, mainlines and departments come from this shared supply, and there are only so many of each. When the last radiator is gone, nobody builds a radiator. Remember that when we talk about order.
steps.cards: These are your market cards. Each one, when played, brings new buyers to a corner of the market you choose. We play one at the end of every year, and I will explain them then.
steps.place-departments: Our two departments start beside the loading bay. In a real game you may drag them anywhere, as long as each touches the bay or the other one. Today we leave them where they stand, so the floor stays clear for the car we are about to build. Tap Done to open the works.
steps.confirm-setup: Confirm, and the works are open.
steps.others-setup: Robin and Sam open their works too. Same floor, same two departments, same nothing.
steps.research: Each year begins with research. It comes first, so whatever we research, we can build and sell later the same year. Your research department gives you one step.
steps.research-rules: A step moves one marker one slot forward. Any marker, on any track, even Robin's or Sam's. Why push a rival? Because the first engineering slot may build whatever another player has researched: patents. I will show you when we set the focus. More departments give more steps, but you may not move the same marker twice in one year. Another player still may.
steps.research-capacity: Or spend the step on your own assembly capacity: how many cars each mainline builds a year. More cars, more dollars. But a car nobody wants is a car nobody buys, so this year we research.
steps.research-clock: Some slots show a punch clock. Reach one, and the timecard moves down a step. Research moves the world on, and the world is running out of time.
steps.research-space: We take reliability. Your marker stands on the battery, and the next slot is the chassis: a big, simple station that gives a car reliability one. Tap the battery, where your marker stands.
steps.research-marker: Three markers stand there. Tap your own, the red one.
steps.research-done: Your marker stands on the chassis. From today you may build a chassis and point a reliability indicator at it. One step, one station: that is the exchange rate.
steps.others-research-robin: Robin takes a step on the safety track, to the brake. Safety is the other track on the market, so a brake sells cars today.
steps.others-research-sam: Sam goes off the board: a step on design, to the paint shop. Nobody can sell design today, so why? Because at the end of the year one track leaves the market, and the off-board track with the most research takes its place. Sam is betting on design. Remember it.
steps.focus: Now we set the focus: the order of play for the year. The focus track runs from engineering on the left to sales on the right. Slot 1 builds first and holds the patents. The last open slot sells first. With three of us, slots 4 and 5 stay closed.
steps.focus-patents: Your slot also decides what you may copy. Slot 1 may build any station that someone else has researched. Slot 2 may build only what both of the others have researched. Slot 3 builds from its own research alone. And when the supply runs short, slot 1 is served first, then slot 2.
steps.focus-gantt: Who chooses first? Whoever has the most Gantt charts. Taking a slot spends all your Gantt charts, back to zero. Passing keeps them, and you take whatever slot is left. A chart saved this year buys a better choice next year.
steps.focus-do: You have the most Gantt charts, so you choose first. Take slot 1. We want to reach the supply before Robin and Sam, and slot 1 is where the patents live.
steps.others-focus-robin: Robin takes slot 3, the sales end. Four buyers and three companies: Robin wants the first pick of them.
steps.others-focus-sam: Sam passes and keeps the Gantt charts. The slot that is left, slot 2, is Sam's. Next year Sam will have the most charts, and choose first.
steps.build: Now we build, everyone at once, each in their own works. The Add gallery holds everything you may build this year. Tap a piece, and it lands on your floor for you to drag into place.
steps.build-rules: Three rules for every tile. It sits on black floor, never on the loading bay. It never overlaps another tile. And it touches the bay, or a tile that does. Anything wrong is outlined in pink until you fix it.
steps.add-mainline: A factory starts with a production line: the mainline. Nothing is built without one. Tap the car mainline in the Add gallery.
steps.place-mainline: Drag the mainline to the ringed spot, beside the loading bay.
steps.mainline: Look at its four sides, marked A, B, C and D: the four steps of building a car. A is the structure. B is the drive. C is the factory options. D is the extras. Each station belongs to one step, and sits against that side.
steps.add-dealer: Cars need somebody to sell them: a dealer. Add your small dealership.
steps.rotate-dealer: Turn it on its side with Rotate, so it fits beside the mainline.
steps.place-dealer: Now drag it against the mainline's left side. A dealer sells the cars of the mainline it touches, so every dealer must touch a mainline, and every mainline a dealer.
steps.dealer-done: Mainline and dealer, touching. This dealer now sells whatever this mainline builds. Today that is a car with no specs at all, and the bottom-left buyers would still take it. But the public will want more soon.
steps.zones: Now a station. The chassis is an A station, so it goes against the A side. See the hatching: every step has its own pattern, and a station, its indicators and the mainline side of the same step form one manufacturing zone.
steps.zones-rule: One rule about zones: two identical stations may never share one. One chassis per zone, one brake per zone. Want two chassis? Give them different sides, or different mainlines.
steps.place-chassis: Drag it below the mainline, against the A side.
steps.add-spec: A station alone does nothing. It needs a spec indicator pointing at it: the proof that we know how to build it well. Your reliability research allows one reliability indicator on the chassis. Tap Add spec.
steps.place-spec: The indicator lands on a free square touching the chassis. Drag it to the ringed square, on the chassis's left, beside the mainline: that keeps the right side free for next year. It could go on any square touching the chassis, as long as it stays in the chassis's zone.
steps.spec-done: That is a spec. Every car off this mainline now has reliability one, because one reliability indicator sits in its zones. Two indicators would be reliability two. That is how a car gets its numbers.
steps.paint-why: One more station, and slot 1 pays for it. Slot 1 may build anything another player has researched, and Sam's marker stands on paint, the first slot of design. Design is not on the market yet, so paint earns nothing this year. But Sam is betting that design comes, and next year we may not hold slot 1. Build it while we can.
steps.move-dealer: Paint is a C station, so it goes against side C, the left, and that is where the dealer stands. Anything you placed this year can still move, so drag the dealer down to the ringed spot. It still touches the mainline, by one square, and one is enough.
steps.rotate-paint: Rotate it, so it lies flat.
steps.place-paint: Drag it against the mainline's left side, above the dealer.
steps.paint-spec: Its spec is design. You never researched design, but slot 1 may use Sam's slot for the indicator as well. Tap Add spec.
steps.place-paint-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, above the paint.
steps.paint-done: Every car off this mainline now has design one as well. It counts for nothing until design reaches the market. Sam thinks it will.
steps.marketing-why: Last, the dealer. A dealer sells through a market window: a frame it lays on the market, and it sells into one niche inside the frame. A small dealer alone has a window of two niches. A marketing department beside it makes the window two by two: more niches, more choice of buyer.
steps.place-marketing: And drag it below the dealer. Marketing must touch a dealer: that is the dealer it serves.
steps.expansion: One last thing, and it is free. Each year you add a floor expansion: more black floor for next year. It came with its own loading bay, and the strip beside that bay must stay clear of tiles, so the door can open. We cannot build on it until next year.
steps.done-build: Nothing is outlined in pink, so everything is legal. Tap Done.
steps.others-build: Robin and Sam build too. Where two of us want the same piece, the supply goes in engineering order: you, then Sam, then Robin.
steps.others-build-look: Look at what Robin built. Three new stations, each with its own spec indicator: a brake and a window pane for safety, and a battery for reliability.
steps.others-build-robin-specs: Each indicator is one point of spec. Two for safety and one for reliability: Robin's cars will read safety two, reliability one. That reaches buyers further along the safety axis than yours can.
steps.others-build-sam: Sam built a brake and a battery: safety one, reliability one. And Sam added a second research department.
steps.others-build-research: So did Robin. Every research department is one research step a year. From next year Robin and Sam each take two steps, and you still take one.
steps.brochures: Now every company prints its sales brochures: the leaflets that tell buyers what each dealer can sell this year. Nobody decides anything here; it all follows from the factories. First the planning. Each planning department adds one Gantt chart. Reaching ten on the track punches the clock.
steps.brochures-specs: Then every dealer publishes what it can sell. Its specs are the indicators in its mainline's zones: yours says reliability one and safety zero, and design one, which no buyer asks for yet. Its window is two by two, thanks to the marketing department beside it.
steps.brochures-reach: The faint rectangle on the market is every niche your dealer could reach this year: the niches that ask for no more than reliability one and no safety at all.
steps.sell: Then we sell, and here the order matters. Sales order runs from the right of the focus track: slot 3 first, then slot 2, then slot 1. On each turn a player must sell if they can, from one dealer, into one niche.
steps.sell-price: What is a buyer worth? That depends on where it stands. The shading cuts the market into four price segments: the cheapest band at the bottom-left, then the second band, then the third band, and the most expensive at the top-right. Each segment's price marker shows what its buyers pay.
steps.sell-price-why: Only the bottom-left segment has buyers today, so it holds the six dollar marker: the best price always goes to the most expensive segment with anybody in it. When buyers appear higher up, this corner's price will fall. The easy buyers are the easy money, but only while nobody else wants them.
steps.sell-window-rule: A window may only cover niches your dealer can satisfy: nothing inside it may ask for more than your specs. It may hang off the edge of the board, and it may overlap another window. Once placed, it stays for the year.
steps.others-sell-robin: Robin sells first, from the sales end of the focus track. The window goes down, and Robin sells one car from it: six dollars.
steps.others-sell-sam: Then Sam lays a window and sells one car too. Two buyers gone, two left.
steps.sell-window: Your turn. Drag your dealer's window onto the ringed spot. It covers the two buyers left, and they ask for nothing, so they are yours to sell to. Then confirm.
steps.sell-niche: Two buyers sit inside your window, in two niches. Your mainline builds one car a year, so you may sell one. Pick either niche.
steps.sold: Six dollars, beside your name. That was your whole capacity for the year: one mainline, one car. Selling goes round in rounds until nobody can sell any more, and nobody may pass while they still can. Robin and Sam are out of cars too, so the selling is over.
steps.finish: Is the game over? Not yet. The timecard decides: when it reaches the last space of the punch clock it flips over, and the game ends after that year. If the clock never runs out, the game ends after the seventh year, when the floor expansions are all used up.
steps.expectations: Now the public changes its mind. The black arrow pointed at safety all year, and safety is leaving the market. It goes under the off-board tracks, and its axis comes off the board.
steps.expectations-min: But safety does not stop mattering. Its minimum specification rises to one, and this marker beside the market says so. From now on no car sells without safety one. Robin and Sam built brakes last year. Your dealer has none. Remember that.
steps.expectations-new: Which track takes its place? The off-board track where research has run furthest past its innovation marker. Sam's design step is the only research off the board, so design enters the market, and Sam already has a step on it. Your paint is ready for it too.
steps.expectations-arrow: The arrow turns to reliability: next year, reliability leaves, and its minimum rises. Plan for it.
steps.grow: Last, demand grows. Each of us plays one market card face down beside a quadrant of the market. The market is cut into four quadrants: one at the bottom-left, two at the bottom-right, three at the top-left and four at the top-right.
steps.grow-neutral: These black cards came first, face down: the neutral deck's. They belong to nobody, and in each quadrant they turn over last.
steps.grow-cards: Here is your hand. Every card is a map of one quadrant of the market. Each car on it is a spark: a niche in that quadrant where the public is warming to cars.
steps.grow-sparks: A spark brings a new buyer to its niche every year. So you play a card where your dealer can reach, and next year the buyers are waiting for you.
steps.grow-clocks: Some cards also punch the clock. Each clock on a card moves the timecard down one step, and brings the end of the game nearer.
steps.grow-year: The number in a card's bottom corner is its year. This one says three: you may play it once you have placed three floor expansions. You have placed one, so today only your year one cards will do. Bigger cards for bigger factories.
steps.play-card: Play this card. It shows one car spark and one punch clock.
steps.play-quadrant: Put it beside quadrant one, where your dealer can reach.
steps.others-cards: Sam and Robin play theirs, face down. Nobody knows where the others' sparks will land until the cards turn.
steps.reveal-sparks: The cards turn over, quadrant by quadrant, one at a time, the black ones last. Each spark flies off its card onto its niche and stays there for good, and every punch clock on a card moves the timecard down.
steps.reveal-buyers: Every spark brings one new buyer, up to two buyers per spark. There they are.
steps.reveal-neutral: Then the black cards. They have no sparks: each brings one buyer of its own, straight onto the niche it shows.
steps.reveal-prices: And the prices are set again: the segment nearest the top-right that has buyers takes the six dollar marker, the next one the four, and so on down.
steps.year-two: That was a whole year. The second goes the same way, and this time you do more of it. Look at your dealer: safety now has a minimum of one, and it has none. It cannot sell a thing until you build a brake.
steps.year-two-why: We could have built one last year. Anybody may: the brake is the first slot of the safety track, and every marker started there. We spent the year on the chassis and the paint instead, and now we pay for it with a brake this year. Every station is a choice; remember that too.
steps.y2-research: Research first, as always. Your marker stands on the chassis, and one step more is the car body: a second reliability indicator, so reliability two. Why two? Look at the market. Two buyers stand together in the second segment, at six dollars each, and they ask for reliability two and no design. Nobody else can reach them today. Tap the chassis, where your marker stands.
steps.y2-research-done: Your marker is on the car body. The punch clocks wait on slots four and six; not this year.
steps.y2-others-research-sam: Sam researches before Robin this year: the order is last year's engineering order, you, then Sam, then Robin. Sam has two research departments now, so two steps. Design again, to the windscreen: design is on the market now, and Sam's bet is paying off. The second step raises Sam's assembly capacity to two: from now on each of Sam's mainlines builds two cars a year.
steps.y2-others-research-robin: Robin, two steps as well. The first goes off the board, to range: a bet on the next track to enter. The second raises Robin's capacity to two as well. Two steps, two different markers: nobody may move one marker twice in a year, though someone else still may.
steps.y2-focus: Now the focus. Sam kept a Gantt chart last year and earned another: two. You and Robin have one each. Sam chooses first.
steps.y2-others-focus-sam: Sam takes slot 1. Why? Patents. Slot 1 may build anything another player has researched: your chassis, Robin's window pane. Sam has no station of its own to build, but it can copy everybody else's.
steps.y2-focus-do: Now you. You and Robin are tied on charts, and a tie goes to whoever had the better engineering slot last year: you. Take slot 3, the sales end. You sell first this year, before Robin and Sam reach the buyers.
steps.y2-others-focus-robin: Robin takes slot 2, the only slot left; passing would have given Robin the same slot, and kept the chart. From slot 2, Robin may copy only what both you and Sam have researched.
steps.y2-build: Build. The expansion you placed last year is floor now; you may build on it, as long as its keep-clear strip stays empty. Everything from last year is fixed where it stands. Two stations today: the brake and the car body.
steps.y2-add-brake: First the brake: a B station, so it goes on the mainline's side B, the right. Add the brake.
steps.y2-place-brake: Drag it against the right side of the mainline, below the loading bay.
steps.y2-brake-spec: It needs its spec indicator. Your safety marker has stood on the brake slot since the start, so you may add a safety indicator. Tap Add spec.
steps.y2-place-brake-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, touching the brake. It is a B indicator, so it joins the brake's zone, and the mainline's side B with it.
steps.y2-add-carbody: Now the car body, an A station. It must join an A zone, but it need not touch the mainline itself: a station touching another station of the same step joins that station's zone, and the chassis's zone already reaches the mainline. Add the car body.
steps.y2-place-carbody: Drag it beside the chassis, on the ringed spot.
steps.y2-carbody-spec: And its indicator: reliability three, the slot you reached this morning. Tap Add spec.
steps.y2-place-carbody-spec: Drag it to the ringed square, touching the car body.
steps.y2-spec-done: Count the indicators in the mainline's zones: two reliability, one safety, one design. Every car off this line now has reliability two, safety one and design one. Your dealer meets the minimum again, and it can sell higher up the board than anyone.
steps.y2-second-why: One more thing, and it is the big one. Two buyers wait at six dollars, but your mainline builds one car a year. A second mainline touching your dealer gives the dealer two cars to sell, and last year's expansion has room for it.
steps.y2-rotate-mainline: Tap Rotate twice, until its C side faces right.
steps.y2-place-mainline: Drag it onto the expansion, to the ringed spot: its C side against the paint, and its corner against the dealer.
steps.y2-shared-dealer: Now your dealer touches two mainlines. On every spec, a dealer publishes the lower of its mainlines. This new line has no stations of its own yet, so look at the dealer's cubes: reliability and safety read zero now. A second line on the same dealer needs the specs of the first, or it drags the dealer down.
steps.y2-shared-zones: But design still reads one. Two lines may share stations: a zone that touches both mainlines counts for both. The paint sits between them, against both C sides, so the new line has design one already. And we could not build paint today: from slot 3 we may build only what we researched ourselves. Last year's slot 1 is paying off.
steps.y2-add-chassis: Reliability first, on the A side, the top. A second chassis is allowed: the same station may be built twice, as long as each copy sits in a different zone. Add the chassis.
steps.y2-rotate-chassis: Rotate it once, so it lies along the top.
steps.y2-place-chassis: Drag it against the mainline's top side.
steps.y2-chassis-spec: And its reliability indicator. Tap Add spec.
steps.y2-place-chassis-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, beside the chassis.
steps.y2-add-brake2: Then safety, on side B, the left. Add the brake.
steps.y2-place-brake2: Drag it beside the mainline, onto the ringed spot.
steps.y2-place-brake2-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, beside the brake.
steps.y2-battery-why: Last, a second reliability point, from a battery on side C. Side C is the paint's zone, and it touches both lines, so a battery there counts for both. It need not touch the paint: it may stand back. A zone runs through indicators as well as stations, so a battery behind the paint's indicator joins the zone.
steps.y2-place-battery: Drag it to the ringed spot, behind the paint's indicator.
steps.y2-place-battery-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, between the battery and the paint.
steps.y2-second-done: Count again. The new line has two reliability, from its chassis and the battery, one safety, and the paint's design. The battery counts for the first line too, which now has reliability three. Your dealer publishes the lower of the two: its cubes are back, and now it has two cars a year to sell.
steps.y2-done-build: This year's expansion is already down where it fits. You may drag it anywhere it touches the factory along the grid, covers no keep-clear strip, and leaves its own strip free. It is fine where it is. Tap Done.
steps.y2-others-build: Robin and Sam build. Sam builds first this year, from slot 1, then Robin, then you: that only matters when the supply runs short, and today it does not.
steps.y2-others-build-look: Look at Robin's factory. A second mainline, out on last year's expansion, with a dealer, a brake and a battery of its own. Two mainlines at capacity two: four cars a year.
steps.y2-others-build-sam: Sam did the same: a second mainline and dealer. Sam also added a windscreen and a paint shop: design two, which reaches the right half of the board.
steps.y2-others-build-yours: But nobody else reads reliability two, so the two buyers at six dollars are yours alone.
steps.y2-brochures: Brochures. One Gantt chart each. Your dealer now publishes reliability two, safety one, design one, with a medium window. Look at Robin's first dealer: it read safety two last year and reads safety one now, because it touches two mainlines, and a dealer publishes the lower of their specs. See how far up the market your reach goes now.
steps.y2-sell-window: You sell first this year. Drag the window to the ringed spot, two rows higher than last year. The two buyers at the top of it ask for reliability two and no design, and you have all of that. With only one niche to sell into, the sale happens the moment you confirm.
steps.y2-sold: Twelve dollars: both buyers at six, one car from each mainline, through one dealer. That is what a second mainline is for. The capacity track is the other way: each step on it is one more car a year from every mainline you own.
steps.y2-others-sell-robin: Robin sells next, in the bottom-left corner: two buyers in one niche, and capacity two, so two cars at once. Eight dollars, four each: buyers appeared higher up, so the corner's price fell, as I warned you.
steps.y2-others-sell-sam: Sam reaches across the board: design two opens the columns on the right, and the buyer there pays six.
steps.y2-sell-rounds: Another round, in the same order. You have no car left. Robin's dealer sells again, one more car in the corner, for four: a dealer sells from its window every round until its mainlines are out of cars. Sam's second dealer has no buyer it can reach, so the selling is over, and the windows come home. With two windows of your own you could sell from either, and where both cover a niche you choose which dealer sells.
steps.y2-finish: The timecard is still far from the end of the clock. On we go.
steps.y2-expectations: The public changes its mind again. Reliability leaves the market, and its minimum becomes one. You have two; Robin and Sam have one each, just enough. Everybody keeps selling, this time.
steps.y2-expectations-tie: Which track enters? Range and safety are tied: Robin has one step past the innovation marker on each. A tie goes to the track that lies higher in the off-board stack, and range lies on top.
steps.y2-expectations-new: Robin's bet paid, and Robin starts the new track one step ahead of everyone. The arrow turns to design: design leaves next year, and its minimum will be one. Only Sam and you have any: your paint, from slot 1.
steps.y2-others-cards: Demand grows, and the cards go down in engineering order: Sam, then Robin, then you. They play face down, so you will not know where their sparks fall until the cards turn.
steps.y2-grow: Your turn. You have two floor expansions now, so you may play a card of year two. Play this one: two sparks and two punch clocks. Two sparks is two new buyers a year, every year, where you can reach them.
steps.y2-play-quadrant: Beside quadrant one again: your dealer can reach its left half.
steps.y2-reveal: The cards turn, and the sparks land: two from your card, two from Robin's beside yours, two from Sam's in quadrant two. The clock punches twice for your card, and twice for Robin's.
steps.y2-reveal-buyers: Then the buyers come: one per spark, up to two per spark on a niche. Nine new buyers this year.
steps.y2-reveal-neutral: Then the three black cards bring their three buyers.
steps.y2-reveal-prices: Then the prices. The second segment keeps the six, and the corner keeps the four, because both still have buyers.
steps.year-three: Two years, director, and you know every rule in the book. What is left is judgement. Research what the market will want next year, not this year. Build a second mainline, or raise your capacity, as soon as you have more buyers than cars. Take slot 1 when the supply is short, or to copy what somebody else researched; the sales end when the buyers are. And save a Gantt chart when passing costs you nothing.
steps.game-end: The game ends after the year in which the timecard flips, or after year seven. Then the richest company wins. If two are tied, the one with the higher sales focus wins.
steps.full-game: We played the introductory rules. In the full game, trucks and sports cars come to market too: a truck pays one dollar more, and a sports car two, but each needs its own, bigger mainline, and those stayed in the box today.
steps.finish-tutorial: The works are yours, director. Build boldly, sell hard. If I can dream it, you can do it!

hints.place-departments: Tap Done in the bar below.
hints.research-space: Tap the highlighted space on the reliability track.
hints.research-marker: Tap your red marker in the gallery.
hints.focus-do: Tap slot 1 on the focus track.
hints.add-mainline: Tap Add in the bar below, then the car mainline.
hints.place-mainline: Drag the mainline onto the ringed spot.
hints.add-dealer: Tap Add, then the small dealership.
hints.place-dealer: Drag the dealer onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-chassis: Drag the chassis onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.move-dealer: Drag the dealer onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-paint: Drag the paint onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-paint-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.add-marketing: Tap Add, then the marketing department.
hints.place-marketing: Drag it onto the ringed spot.
hints.sell-window: Drag the window above the board onto the ringed spot, then tap Confirm.
hints.sell-niche: Tap one of the highlighted niches inside your window.
hints.play-quadrant: Tap the ringed space beside quadrant one.
hints.y2-research: Tap the chassis slot on the reliability track.
hints.y2-focus-do: Tap slot 3 on the focus track.
hints.y2-place-brake: Drag the brake onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-brake-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-add-carbody: Tap Add, then the car body.
hints.y2-place-carbody: Drag the car body onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-carbody-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-sell-window: Drag the window above the board onto the ringed spot, then tap Confirm.
hints.y2-play-quadrant: Tap the ringed space beside quadrant one.
hints.y2-add-mainline: Tap Add, then the car mainline.
hints.y2-rotate-mainline: Tap Rotate until the C side faces right.
hints.y2-place-mainline: Drag the mainline onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-chassis: Drag the chassis onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-chassis-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-place-brake2: Drag the brake onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-brake2-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-place-battery: Drag the battery onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-battery-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
